This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'M.V.Act') has been filed
aggrieved by award dated 25/01/2017 passed by the 1st Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Bharat Lal Dewar vs Gajendra Bareth on 16 January, 2024

1

Sakti, District - Janjgir- Champa (Cg) in Claim Case No.08/2016.

2. By the impugned award, learned Tribunal has awarded Rs.25,000/- in favour of the
appellants/claimants as compensation on account of death of Jageshwar Dewar in an unfortunate
accident that took place on 20/09/2015 by rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle
(Truck Hyva) bearing registration No.CG-13/LA/3991 by respondent No.1/driver, owned by
respondent No.2/owner and insured with respondent No.3/insurance company.
3.  The appellants / claimants filed an application under Section 166 of the MV Act claiming compensation of Rs.21,90,000/-.
As per pleadings of the claim application, the deceased was aged about 53 years and he was earning Rs.10,000/- as monthly income as Confectioner (Halwai).
Therefore, the said compensation was claimed.

The appellants / claimants are elder brother,
sister-in-law and nephews of the deceased.

Respondents filed their written statement and resisted the claim application on various grounds and the insurance company stated that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license and the appellants / claimants are not dependents of the deceased.
Therefore, the insurance company is not liable to pay compensation.
4. Learned Tribunal framed 4 issues on the basis of pleadings and decided those issues in favour of the appellants/claimants.
5. Learned counsel for the appellants / claimants argues that the monthly income of the deceased has been assessed on the lower side and the amount of compensation awarded is also on the lower side.

6. Learned counsel for respondent No.2 submits that the accident was not occurred by the offending vehicle and if the appellants / claimants are entitled for compensation, the insurance company is liable to pay the same.
7. Learned counsel for respondent / insurance company submits that the appellants / claimants are not entitled to any compensation as they are not dependents of the deceased.
8. I have heard learned counsel for the parties, considered their rival submissions and perused the records.

9. Learned Tribunal has awarded Rs.25,000/- (Rs.20,000/- for love and affection & Rs.5,000/- for funeral) as compensation in favour of the appellants / claimants holding that appellants are distant relatives of the deceased.
They are not dependent on the deceased and they are major aged about 55 years, 50 years, 35 years and 30 years respectively.
From their statement, it is reflected that they are not dependent upon the income of the deceased.

Therefore, the finding of the learned Tribunal does not appear to be perverse or contrary to the records, however, this Court is inclined to award Rs.40,000/- towards filial consortium to appellant No.1 and Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate.
The total compensation comes to Rs.55,000/- to be paid by respondent No.3 within a period of 60 days.
